requirements.title: Pointer actual arguments to nonoptional nonpointer dummies must be associated except for inquiry references
requirements.definition: Except in references to intrinsic inquiry functions, a pointer actual argument for a nonoptional nonpointer dummy argument is pointer associated with a target.

pending.associated-pointer-actual-control: Associate integer pointer p with target t initialized to 71, pass p to a nonoptional nonpointer dummy, and expect the callee observes 71 in sentinel -71.
pending.disassociated-pointer-actual-source: Source-control negative NULLIFYs p before the same call; positive control associates p with t. This unnumbered program restriction has no required diagnostic claim.
pending.intrinsic-inquiry-exception: Use ASSOCIATED on a disassociated pointer actual and expect .FALSE. in a logical sentinel initialized to .TRUE.; this covers only the intrinsic inquiry exception.

requirements.title: A VALUE dummy is associated with a definable anonymous object initialized from the actual value
requirements.definition: A present VALUE dummy becomes argument associated with a definable anonymous data object whose initial value is the actual argument value.

pending.value-dummy-initial-value: Pass integer actual a=17 to a VALUE dummy; inside copy entry value to result sentinel -1 and expect 17.
pending.value-dummy-definable-anonymous-object: Inside a no-INTENT VALUE dummy procedure, assign dummy=29 and record local value 29 before return, proving a definable object rather than expression-only value.
pending.value-dummy-caller-unchanged: After the VALUE dummy is assigned 29 locally, expect caller actual a remains 17 and a separate call-count sentinel confirms the procedure executed.

requirements.title: Pointer dummy argument association depends on whether the actual argument is a pointer
requirements.definition: A present pointer dummy corresponding to a pointer actual becomes argument associated with that actual; a present pointer dummy corresponding to a nonpointer actual is not argument associated.

requirements.title: The ultimate argument follows effective-argument chains and dummy subobjects
requirements.definition: The ultimate argument is the effective argument unless that effective argument is a dummy argument or subobject of a dummy argument; in those cases the ultimate argument is found recursively, preserving corresponding subobject selection.
